title: Beyond screen time: The core influences of problematic screen use on adolescent development networks
authors: Xu LX, Song KR, Deng HY, Geng XM, Zhang JL, Fang XY, Potenza MN, Zhang JT

primary_models.name: Cross-lagged panel network (LASSO-regularized regressions) of T4 psychopathology, behavioral tendencies and environment on T2 problematic social media and mobile phone use, female network, covariate-residualized
primary_models.location_in_paper: Female CLPN: Results text pp. 730-731 ('The impact of problematic screen use on individual development'); Fig. 4B (left) and Fig. 4C (p. 732); full edge list in supplementary eTable 10 (not in PDF). Interpreted in Discussion pp. 732-733.
primary_models.design: Longitudinal two-wave cross-lagged panel network (CLPN). Predictors are the 20 nodes measured at the ABCD 2-year follow-up (T2, ages 11-12, 2018-2020); outcomes are the same 20 nodes at the 4-year follow-up (T4, ages 13-14, 2020-2022). Each T4 node is regressed on all 20 T2 nodes, including its own T2 value (autoregressive path), so each cross-lagged coefficient is the prediction of a T4 node by a T2 node adjusted for all other T2 nodes. The 20 nodes are 3 problematic-use nodes (A1 problematic video game, A2 problematic social media, A3 problematic mobile phone), 8 CBCL syndrome scales (C1-C8), 3 behavioral-tendency nodes (UPPS, BIS, BAS) and 6 environmental nodes (E1-E6). Screen-time and phone-checking nodes from the cross-sectional networks were not carried into the CLPN. 20 x 19 = 380 possible cross-lagged edges per network. Single follow-up, no repeated measures beyond the two waves. Networks estimated separately by sex.
primary_models.sample: ABCD Release 5.1. Youth with data at both the 2-year (T2) and 4-year (T4) follow-up; one child randomly selected per family. Total CLPN sample N = 3,954 (abstract and Table 1); this female network N = 1,863 (47.12% of the CLPN sample). Females: age at T2 143.21 months (SD 7.77), age at T4 168.53 months (SD 7.88). Race: White 1,250 (67%), Black 225 (12%), Asian 52 (2.8%), mixed/other 336 (18%). Hispanic 394 (21%), non-Hispanic 1,469 (79%). Parents married/living with partner 1,400 (75%); parental education college 1,420 (76%); family income <$25,000 274 (15%) through $200,000+ 207 (11%) (Table 1, p. 727).
primary_models.iv: Problematic use at T2, entered as continuous scale scores. A2 = Social Media Addiction Questionnaire (SMAQ); A3 = Mobile Phone Involvement Questionnaire (MPIQ; Walsh, White, & Young, 2010). Missing problematic-use items due to not meeting prerequisites (no social media account, no mobile phone) were imputed with the minimum scale value ("never"); other missing data imputed with predictive mean matching in the CLPN. All variables were residualized on covariates and the standardized residuals entered the network. Descriptive statistics for SMAQ/MPIQ are not in the main PDF (supplementary materials only). A1 (problematic video game, VGAQ) is also a T2 predictor node but is not a qualifying modality.
primary_models.dv: T4 nodes on the other side of the cross-lagged edge. CBCL syndrome scales, caregiver-report (C1 anxious/depressed, C2 withdrawn/depressed, C3 somatic complaints, C4 social problems, C5 thought problems, C6 attention problems, C7 rule-breaking, C8 aggressive); impulsivity from the brief UPPS-P (UPPS); Behavioral Inhibition (BIS) and Behavioral Activation (BAS) from the BIS/BAS scale; environmental factors E1 family conflict (FES conflict subscale), E2 prosocial peer involvement (Peer Behavior Profile, reverse scored), E3 delinquent peer involvement / peer rule-break (Peer Behavior Profile), E4 perceived school environment (SRPF, reverse scored, so higher = more adverse), E5 positive school involvement (SRPF, reverse scored, so higher = less involvement), E6 school disengagement (SRPF). Whether CBCL raw or T-scores were used is not stated. All entered as standardized residuals after covariate adjustment.

primary_models.equation: node_j,T4[i] = b0 + a_j*node_j,T2[i] + sum_{k != j} b_jk*node_k,T2[i] + e[i], estimated for each of the 20 T4 nodes, with all nodes as standardized residuals after regressing on age, race, ethnicity, parental marital status, parental education and family income. Focal coefficients: b_j,A2 (problematic social media at T2 -> node j at T4) and b_j,A3 (problematic mobile phone at T2 -> node j at T4). Coefficients are LASSO-penalized (L1) so small coefficients are shrunk to exactly zero.
primary_models.estimation: R (glmnet for LASSO; qgraph for plotting; bootnet; NetworkComparisonTest). LASSO-penalized maximum-likelihood regression with 10-fold cross-validation to select the tuning parameter. No random effects or weights; one child randomly selected per family to ensure independence. Missing data: minimum-value imputation for structurally missing problematic-use items, predictive mean matching for remaining missingness (MCAR per Little's test, eFigs 2-4). No p-values, confidence intervals or multiple-comparison correction are reported for individual cross-lagged edges; edges reported in text are non-zero LASSO coefficients and the authors describe them as significant associations. Mean autoregressive B: female 0.406, male 0.391; mean cross-lagged B: female 0.012, male 0.013. Stability via CS coefficients (eFig. 12); female/male network structure correlation r = 0.47, t = 10.382, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.39, 0.55]. Sensitivity analyses with pairwise deletion and categorical problematic-use indicators reported only in supplementary eFigs 18 and 21 (narrative: results stable). Sex differences handled by stratification; no formal sex x edge test for the CLPN.

d_transformation.native_metric: other:CLPN cross-lagged edge (LASSO-penalized regression coefficient B on standardized residuals)
d_transformation.conversion_formula: None applied. If a reviewer chooses to treat the coefficient as an approximate standardized beta, the guidelines' beta_std -> d formula would be d = 2*beta / sqrt(1 - beta^2), but this is not recommended (see notes).
d_transformation.contrast_type: Per 1 SD of the covariate-residualized problematic-use score at T2, conditional on all other 19 T2 nodes (inferred from use of standardized residuals; not stated explicitly for the regression outputs).
d_transformation.notes: Coefficients are cross-lagged network edges from LASSO-penalized regressions with 10-fold CV, so they are shrunk toward zero and conditional on 19 other predictors, including the autoregressive T2 value. No SEs, CIs or p-values are reported, and SDs of SMAQ/MPIQ and the outcomes are not in the main PDF (Table 1 gives demographics only). Per guidelines, network edge weights are treated as non-convertible; these papers go to a later review level. Only edges printed in the Results text are extracted; Fig. 4B hides edges with |B| < 0.05, and the full matrix is in supplementary eTable 10, which is not bundled in the PDF.

extraction_flags:
1. Where the numbers come from: every estimate is a B copied from the Results text on pp. 730-731. The paper has no results table, and the full edge matrix is in supplementary eTable 10, which is not in the PDF. Fig. 4B hides edges with |B| < 0.05. So only the edges the authors chose to report in the text are extracted. There may be other A2/A3 edges that are non-zero but not reported.

2. pdftotext drops minus signs. I checked the page image: A2→C5 in the female network is B = −0.251. The positive signs on the other A2/A3 edges match the narrative text.

3. No SE, CI or p-value is reported for any edge. I set sig=true on every estimate on the basis that the edge is non-zero after LASSO and the authors describe these as significant associations. A coder should decide whether that is acceptable.

4. The male A2→C1 edge is printed with the symbol β instead of B (0.113). I assume it is the same metric as the other edges.

5. On d_transformable=false: the paper says covariate-residualized standardized residuals were used, so the coefficients may in effect be in SD units. However, they are LASSO-shrunk and conditional on 19 other T2 nodes, including the autoregressive term. Following the rule that network edges are non-convertible, I marked the paper not transformable. A coder could choose to treat them as approximate beta_std instead.

6. E4 (perceived school environment) and E5 (positive school involvement) are reverse-scored. A positive B therefore means a more adverse school environment and lower school involvement. Whether perceived school environment counts as an individual-trait or a contextual variable should be checked.

7. Cross-sectional GGM edges involving social media time (B2), checking (B3), A2 and A3 with CBCL/UPPS/BIS/BAS appear only in figures (Fig. 2A, Fig. 3) and in supplementary eTables 8-9. I excluded them rather than read values off the figures. A coder may want to pull eTable 8 from the online supplement.

8. Whether CBCL raw scores or T-scores were used is not stated. The PDF reports no SDs for SMAQ, MPIQ or the outcomes.
